thread:
Lena Ortiz: Orchid Wharf week0 blockers 1 audit log shape + destination, 2) customer CMK ownership & rotation. Need both confirmed to proceed with Tue cutover. Can we close today?

Harold Finch: I can do a quick check. Do they have an example audit event? JSONL preferred?

Lena Ortiz: They sent a sample and said single-line JSONL per event. Pasting for runbook record:
```json
{"evt_id":"evt-20260321-01","tenant":"orchid-wharf","ts":"2026-03-21T08:04:12Z","type":"inference","model":"rwd-6b","prompt_tokens":64,"resp_tokens":120,"lat_ms":92,"redacted":true}
```

Priya Desai: KMS notes from their sec team: CMK must be in their AWS account, rotation every 45 days (tight), and they will manage rotation. They want us to have cryptographic usage only (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey). No Admin or key policy edit rights. They also asked for aliasing so the config can point to an alias and not need an ARN swap on rotation.

Harold Finch: Ok. We'll ask them to include a statement denying kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion and kms:DisableKey for our principal. Also include condition to restrict key usage to requests originating from their VPC endpoint ID and our principal ARN. I'll draft the policy snippet.

security-bot: Security checklist (auto): - Audit logs MUST include tenant + evt_id + ts. - Strip PII before ingest; set redaction=true flag. - KMS key policy: customer-admin only; grant our service principal only crypto actions. - Require TLS with client cert for log forwarder.

Harold Finch: Draft KMS key policy snippet (for their security to paste):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/orchid-security-admin"},"Action":"kms:*","Resource":"*"},
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/redwood-service-principal"},"Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555666777888:key/abcd-1234","Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:SourceVpce":"vpce-0a1b2c3d"}}},
    {"Effect":"Deny","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111222333444:role/redwood-service-principal"},"Action":["kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion","kms:DisableKey"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:555666777888:key/abcd-1234"}
  ]
}
```

Lena Ortiz: Networking: Orchids have a strict outbound allowlist. They will accept logs only from three static IPs. They asked which public IPs our Private appliance will present. Options: (A) customer-side NAT with Elastic IPs (preferred), (B) our dedicated egress NAT (needs approval). We need to confirm which one they'll use.

infra-bot: onboarding-checklist updated by Harold Finch: added "audit-jsonl-sample", "customer-cmk-45d", "egress-static-ips".

Priya Desai: If they use customer NAT (A), we just publish the internal endpoint hostname; if (B) we expose our egress IPs and they'll add them to allowlist. We should ask them to send the three IPs and their collector fqdn and cert fingerprint for mTLS.

Harold Finch: I'm free for a 20-min sync at 15:40 PT to walk through the policy and IPs. Can others join?

Lena Ortiz: 15:40 PT works. Inviting Orchids' security and networking. :calendar:

ops-bot: runbook updated by Lena Ortiz  entries: audit-jsonl-sample, kms-policy-snippet, egress-ips-action-item. Link: https://redwood.internal/onboard/OrchidWharf/runbook (internal)

Priya Desai: After the call I'll post the exact runbook diff and the KMS policy template to their security mailbox. We'll also add a masking step in ingestion for any remaining PII fields.

Lena Ortiz: Thanks all. I'll capture post-call notes here and mark ready-for-cutover once we have: 1) CMK ARN + policy posted by customer, 2) collector FQDN + 3 IPs + cert fingerprint.
